# Quantitative deepest-face exhaustion and a linear buffer-value gap

This note proves the fixed-body statement proposed by the contributor and a quantitative extension to bodies near an ordinary minimum. The extension uses the actual single-input enlargement; it does not transfer a fixed-body estimate to changing bodies by an unquantified continuity argument.

Under the established compact positive minimal-bad-base framework, it yields a two-sided linear estimate for the globally optimized buffered VALUE as epsilon tends to zero. It proves neither differentiability of that value nor existence of a common response separator with an epsilon direction, and gives no Gamma payment.

The geometric input is `candidate cebc39c4f5ccbc96`. The new points here are quantitative near-face exhaustion, domination of a nonnegative concave parameter by near-deepest marks, and the explicit two-envelope argument in Section 6.

## 1. Actual setting and uniform geometric constants

Fix a finite base P and d>=1. Let K_z be positive compatible convex fibers, exactly the sampled fibers of their canonical hull. Write

    M=sum_z |K_z|,
    q_z=max_(y in K_z) ordinaryDepth(z,y),
    Q=max_z q_z,  beta_0=Q/M.

Depth means ORIGINAL raw closed-halfspace depth, including pure-base caps. For p in conv(P), let F_p be its minimal containing base face.

For the quantitative changing-body assertions normalize M=1 and work in a class with fixed constants

    K_z subset R Ball_d,
    |K_z|>=v>0,
    B(o_z,r_b) subset K_z,
    lambda_- I <=Sigma_C<=lambda_+ I,  lambda_->0.     (1)

The centers o_z can be chosen separately. Their use in estimates is not a claim that independent contractions about them are compatible motions. The compact positive family framework supplies (1), after the permitted common continuous affine maps and affine base shears. The buffered functional with the covariance norm and logarithmic parameter normalization is invariant under those maps.

Let m=|P| and omega_j be the volume of the unit j-ball, with omega_0=1. Put

    A=m omega_(d-1) R^(d-1),
    q_*=omega_d r_b^d/2>0.                            (2)

At the center of any displayed inball every containing nonvertical cap captures at least half that ball, while any containing pure-base cap captures its whole own fiber. Thus Q>=q_* uniformly. Ordinary depth within a fixed fiber is A-Lipschitz in the continuous mark, and is zero at its boundary. Boundary zero follows from the finite support-height roof and a global supporting cap with nonzero continuous normal, as in the cited source.

All numerical constants below depend only on P,d and the fixed constants in (1). Their explicit values are intentionally conservative.

## 2. Quantitative single-input enlargement

For u in P replace its INPUT fiber by K_u+t Ball_d and take the actual canonical hull of this fiber and all other old input fibers. Denote the resulting sampled fibers by K_z(t). For 0<t<=1,

    K_z subset K_z(t) subset K_z+t Ball_d,
    K_u(t)=K_u+t Ball_d.                              (3)

The proof is the exact anchored-combination argument from the cited source: the only added displacement is lambda_u t b, of norm at most t. Hence this is a legitimate compatible family with the same projection and integer bases, not an independent motion of all the other fibers.

Since B(o_z,r_b) is contained in K_z,

    K_z+t Ball_d subset o_z+(1+t/r_b)(K_z-o_z).

Consequently, writing Delta_t=M_t-1 for the added mixed volume,

    Delta_t<=C_V t,
    C_V=(d/r_b)(1+1/r_b)^(d-1).                       (4)

For the reverse estimate, every X in K_u is within 2R of o_u, so

    o_u+(1+t/(2R))(K_u-o_u) subset K_u+t Ball_d.

Therefore

    Delta_t >= c_m t,       c_m=d v/(2R)>0.           (5)

For every new mark x_t in K_z(t), choose an old x in K_z within t. Paired nonvertical caps, normalized by Euclidean continuous normal length one, differ in mass by at most Delta_t+A t. Pure-base caps differ by at most Delta_t. Taking infima and then maxima gives

    q_z(t)<=q_z+C_D t,       C_D=C_V+A.               (6)

Only old-fiber section bounds are needed: compare measures first, then shift the threshold on the old body. Thus (6) is uniform in the base tilt and includes all supporting statuses.

If u is outside a base face F, every fiber over F is EXACTLY unchanged: an anchored representation targeting F uses only inputs in F. The exact face-isolation identity makes the ordinary depth at every point over F unchanged as well. Relative face caps extend to ambient closed caps excluding all other finitely many fibers by a finite exposing tilt. This remains valid for singleton faces and pure-base relative caps.

## 3. Near-deepest faces must cover near an ordinary global minimum

Let beta_* be the infimum of beta_0 over ALL positive compatible families on this fixed base, not over an artificially bounded normalization class. For a family satisfying (1), put

    g=beta_0-beta_*=Q-beta_*>=0,
    I_eta={p in P:q_p>=Q-eta}.

If some u lies outside the union of F_p for p in I_eta, perform (3) with

    t=eta/(2C_D),       0<eta<=2C_D.

All bases in I_eta retain their old depths exactly. The others have q_z<Q-eta and, by (6), still have q_z(t)<Q-eta/2. Since all actual deepest bases belong to I_eta, the new raw maximum is EXACTLY Q. Thus, using (4)--(5),

    beta_0(C)-beta_0(C_t)
       =Q Delta_t/(1+Delta_t)
       >=q_* c_m eta/[2C_D(1+C_V)] = c_F eta,         (7)

where

    c_F=q_* c_m/[2C_D(1+C_V)]>0.

The expanded body is a legal competitor for beta_*. It may be renormalized afterward; normalized original depth is unchanged by that renormalization. It need not remain in the particular bounded representative set (1). Hence a missed base implies

    g>=c_F eta.                                      (8)

Choose

    eta_0=min(2C_D,q_*/2),
    g_0=c_F eta_0/2>0.

For every 0<g<=g_0 the minimal faces of I_eta cover P when

    eta=2g/c_F.                                      (9)

Otherwise (8) would give g>=2g, a contradiction. If g=0, the exact deepest-face exhaustion theorem gives the same conclusion with eta=0. This is quantitative coverage of NEAR-deepest faces; it is not a claim that the actual deepest faces cover P at every nonminimizing family.

For each p in this covering set choose a maximizer y_p with depth q_p. Since eta<=q_*/2,

    q_p>=Q-eta>=q_*/2.

The own-boundary zero and the A-Lipschitz estimate therefore put all chosen marks in uniform own balls. A convenient radius is

    r_s=q_*/(4A),       B(y_p,r_s) subset K_p.         (10)

There is no rate assumption on the Hausdorff approach to an ordinary minimizing body; only the ordinary objective gap g appears in (9).

## 4. Concave parameters are controlled by covering face marks

This is an elementary finite-base lemma, also valid at a single fixed body. Suppose J is a set of bases such that their minimal faces cover P, and let Y_p=(p,y_p), p in J, have own inballs of radius r_s. Assume all fibers lie in R Ball_d.

For each ordered pair (p,u) with u in P intersect F_p choose once a finite anchored representation of p with a positive weight t_pu at u. Such a representation exists because p lies in relint F_p: extend the ray from u through p to the opposite boundary of F_p, then express that boundary point by vertices of F_p. If u=p, take t_pp=1. Since there are finitely many pairs, their fixed positive weights have a positive minimum t_*, depending only on P.

Let L be any nonnegative concave function on the actual canonical body, finite at the chosen marks. For any X_u in K_u, use its selected representation and arbitrary points in the other input fibers. The resulting X belongs to K_p and satisfies

    L(p,X)>=t_* L(u,X_u).                             (11)

The nonnegativity of the other input values is used here. Given X in K_p, extend the ray from X through y_p to the opposite point of its own inball. This expresses y_p as a convex combination with weight

    r_s/(r_s+|X-y_p|)>=r_s/(r_s+2R)

at X. Thus

    L(Y_p)>=c_L L(u,X_u),
    c_L=t_* r_s/(r_s+2R)>0.                          (12)

Taking suprema gives the claimed global bound

    sup_S L <=c_L^(-1) max_(p in J) L(Y_p).           (13)

It is valid even without boundary attainment of the supremum. If L is logarithmically normalized, its sampled supremum is at least one. Therefore at least one of the selected marks has L(Y_p)>=c_L. No global affine centroid graph or affine parameter is assumed.

## 5. Uniform linear increase at one selected mark

Use the actual invariant buffer

    epsilon [L(Y) E_(K_p)(y)/M]^(1/N) Gamma_C(u),
    N=d+1, Gamma_C(u)=sqrt(u^T Sigma_C u).

Continue with M=1. At the mark supplied by (12)--(13), its source ball gives

    E_(K_p)(y)>=omega_d r_s^d=:E_min.

Indeed every denominator admissible on K_p is admissible on its own contained ball, whose centroidal projective energy equals its volume. Hence the scalar displacement is at least epsilon d_0, where

    d_0=(c_L E_min)^(1/N)>0.

For Euclidean unit u, the actual normal displacement is at least epsilon d_0 sqrt(lambda_-). The own-ball strip has volume at least

    A_s min(r_s/2,epsilon d_0 sqrt(lambda_-)),
    A_s=omega_(d-1)(sqrt(3)r_s/2)^(d-1).

Every nonvertical buffered cap therefore has at least this much more mass than its unbuffered through-source counterpart. Independently, every pure-base cap has mass at least ordinaryDepth(Y)+V_p/2 by the opposite-continuous-perturbation bound. Set

    c_B=A_s d_0 sqrt(lambda_-)>0,
    epsilon_0=min(r_s/[2d_0 sqrt(lambda_-)], v/[2c_B]). (14)

For 0<epsilon<=epsilon_0, taking the infimum over ALL cap types gives

    bufferedDepth(Y)>=ordinaryDepth(Y)+c_B epsilon.   (15)

This proof requires neither a minimizing cap nor cap regularity. Large values of L(Y) do not invalidate it: they only increase the displacement, and the displayed lower bound is used together with the fixed pure-base margin.

## 6. Fixed-body and genuinely changing-body value bounds

At a FIXED ordinary local minimum, use its exact deepest bases in Sections 4--5. The face-exhaustion theorem supplies their face cover. Choose one deepest interior mark at each of them. After normalizing M=1, the construction gives constants c>0, epsilon_0>0 depending on that body and P such that, for EVERY positive concave log-normalized L,

    beta_epsilon(C,L)>=beta_0(C)+c epsilon
                    for 0<epsilon<=epsilon_0.        (16)

Taking L=1 and the all-normal slab estimate gives beta_epsilon(C,1)<=beta_0(C)+A sqrt(lambda_+) epsilon. Thus the fixed-body infimum over L has an exact two-sided linear scale. No attainment of that parameter infimum is needed for this statement. For unnormalized M, divide the raw depth increments by M and include M in d_0 as in the buffer definition.

For changing bodies in (1), let 0<=g<=g_0 and choose the near-deepest covering marks from Section 3. Equations (9) and (15) give

    beta_epsilon(C,L)>=beta_0(C)-2g/c_F+c_B epsilon.

Set H=max(1,2/c_F). Since buffering never lowers original depth,

    beta_epsilon(C,L)-beta_*
      >=max{g, c_B epsilon-(H-1)g}
      >=c_B epsilon/H.                              (17)

The last inequality is elementary: if g>=c_B epsilon/H use the first term; otherwise use the second. This is the step that deals with an UNKNOWN rate g/epsilon. It is not a substitution of a fixed-body bound at the limiting body.

If g>g_0, the trivial lower bound beta_epsilon>=beta_0 gives the same conclusion whenever epsilon<=H g_0/c_B. Thus every family in the uniform class (1), with every admissible parameter, obeys the positive linear gap for sufficiently small epsilon.

Finally assume the established minimal-bad-base framework: beta_* is below a fixed b, every family with beta_0<=b has a representative satisfying (1), and the competitor class is ALL actual positive compatible families on P. Families outside that sublevel have beta_epsilon>=b, while families inside satisfy (17). Reducing epsilon again so c_B epsilon/H<=b-beta_* proves the global bound

    beta_*+c epsilon <= inf_(C,L) beta_epsilon(C,L)
                     <=beta_*+C epsilon,             (18)

for fixed positive c,C and all sufficiently small epsilon. The upper bound uses L=1 at an ordinary minimizer, whose attainment follows from the same compact framework. Equivalently one may use uniformly normalized ordinary near-minimizers and then take their infimum. The lower bound uses unrestricted ordinary competitors after the single-input expansion; it does not optimize over an artificially compact constrained shape class.

## 7. Retained scope

The fixed-body statement (16) needs ordinary local minimality only through its exact face cover. The joint value statement (18) needs the global ordinary infimum and the uniform compact positive representative framework. The constants are not claimed sharp. This does not assert an optimizer derivative, interchange infima with a first variation, provide a physical separator at near-optimal pairs, or establish any Gamma estimate.

In particular, a proposed additional optimization in epsilon would need its own attained scalar/body/parameter minimum and the actual common response alternative including that scalar direction. Equation (18) alone does not manufacture those ingredients.

## 8. A separate uniform row comparison from the same face estimate

the contributor observed another consequence of Section 4 that does NOT require deepest-face exhaustion. Suppose an actual logarithmic volume certificate has a source Y_i=(p_i,y_i) with its own inball B(y_i,r_s), and an active affine plane A_i>=L>=0 touching there. The tilted probability row rho_i has full mean Y_i and satisfies E_rho_i L=L_i. Its base mean forces it to be supported over the minimal face F_i of p_i. Affine Jensen equality gives L=A_i rho_i-almost everywhere.

Apply the proof of Section 4 to A_i with the single source p_i and the target bases in F_i. Positivity on the canonical body and its source ball gives, uniformly on all of that face's sampled fibers,

    0<=A_i(z,X)/L_i<=C_0,
    C_0=(r_s+2R)/(r_s t_*).

Therefore the original-volume row d bar_rho_i=(L/L_i)d rho_i satisfies the uniform ONE-SIDED comparison

    d bar_rho_i/d rho_i<=C_0,
    0<=KL(bar_rho_i||rho_i)<=log C_0.                 (19)

After averaging by any actual source probabilities sigma_i,

    K_V=sum_i sigma_i KL(bar_rho_i||rho_i)<=log C_0.   (20)

The constant is independent of epsilon, of the parameter's absolute scale, and of the number of repeated source occurrences. This is a bound for actual contact rows; a mere pair of measures with chosen source locations is not sufficient. It does not give the reverse density comparison or make the original-volume row's barycenter equal to Y_i. It supplies no Gamma payment.

The companion `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_quantitative_face_gap_slab_recovery.py` passes 1,316 exact calibration checks. Its body examples are actual two-base interval families; its final checks verify the two-envelope scalar inequality. The checks supplement, rather than replace, the all-body geometric proof.
